2608.21317.title: From Regulation to Implementation: A Critical Evaluation of LLM-Assisted Regulatory Compliance in Industry
2608.21317.paper_summary: The European Union (EU) has emerged as a leading regulatory body in the development of sustainability and privacy regulations. While new regulation requirements vary, many include a documentation artifact to ensure compliance. Notably, the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) introduces Digital Product Passports (DPPs) for life cycle transparency, while the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) mandates Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) to mitigate privacy risks. Creating these compliance artifacts, however, is challenging. Industrial data, which often exists in heterogeneous formats and is scattered across company and supplier systems, is required for DPPs and can be difficult to extract into compliant DPP formatting. Furthermore, DPIA documents require interdisciplinary expertise and follow no standardized format, making development difficult for novel systems. To address the particular complexity of compliance artifact creation for both regulations, researchers have proposed the use of LLMs in the generation process; however, the impact of the aforementioned problems on the output of these systems is largely unaddressed. This work investigates the existing research gap by exploring how data extraction instructions and regulatory vagueness impact the quality and consistency of LLM-produced compliance artifacts. The resulting artifacts are evaluated by benchmarking different models against manually created ground-truth schemas. The results reveal that less strict guidelines, such as DPIA formatting, require higher context prompts to maintain consistency and completeness. Stricter guidelines, such as formatting for Digital Battery Passports (DBP), result in consistent results regardless of prompt context, but may lead to more hallucinations in the output
2608.21317.paper_summary_zh: 歐洲聯盟（EU）已經成為可持續性和隱私法規發展的主要監管機構。雖然新的法規要求各不相同，但許多都包括一個文檔產物以確保合規性。值得注意的是，針對可持續產品的生態設計法規（ESPR）引入了數位產品護照（DPPs）以實現生命週期透明度，而一般數據保護法規（GDPR）則要求進行數據保護影響評估（DPIAs）以減輕隱私風險。然而，創建這些合規性產物是具有挑戰性的。工業數據通常以異構格式存在，並分散在公司和供應商系統中，這些數據是DPP所需的，並且提取為合規的DPP格式可能很困難。此外，DPIA文檔需要跨學科的專業知識，並且沒有標準化格式，這使得新系統的開發變得困難。為了解決這兩項法規的合規性產物創建的特定複雜性，研究人員提出在生成過程中使用大型語言模型（LLMs）；然而，前述問題對這些系統輸出的影響在很大程度上尚未得到解決。本研究通過探討數據提取指令和法規模糊性如何影響LLM產生的合規性產物的質量和一致性，來調查現有的研究空白。所產生的產物通過將不同模型與手動創建的真實基準模式進行基準測試來進行評估。結果顯示，較不嚴格的指導方針，例如DPIA格式，要求更高的上下文提示以維持一致性和完整性。較嚴格的指導方針，例如數位電池護照（DBP）的格式，則無論提示上下文如何都能產生一致的結果，但可能導致輸出中出現更多幻覺。
